rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is against exchanging God’s covenant and the Messenger’s pledge for a small worldly return, such as Quraysh’s offers to weak Muslims to apostatize.
rows.anchor: لا تأخذوا بمقابلة عهده تعالى وبيعة رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything of worldly value, however abundant, perishes, whereas the kinds of mercy stored with God have no end.
rows.anchor: من أعراض الدنيا وإن كثرت

rows.speaker: الجهمية
rows.claim: Bursevī presents the Jahmiyya as claiming that Paradise’s bliss eventually ends, and invokes this verse against their claim.
rows.anchor: وهو حجة على الجهمية لأنهم يقولون بأن نعيم الجنة يتناهى وينقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises a special recompense to those who patiently bear polytheists’ harm and Islam’s hardships, including keeping covenants and poverty.
rows.anchor: على أذية المشركين ومشاق الإسلام التي من جملتها الوفاء بالعهود والفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling their works the best signals the completeness of their goodness; the phrase is not a limitation to some lesser reward.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضيف إليه الأحسن للاشعار بكمال حسنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Keeping faith and covenants and enduring hardship yield benefits both in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: أن للوفاء بالعهد والثبات على الإيمان والصبر على المشاق ثمرات دنيوية وأخروية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wise should not break their covenant with God, nor their commitments to practicing scholars and perfected righteous people.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن لا ينقض المعاهدة التي بينه بين الله وكذا بين العلماء العاملين والصلحاء الكاملين

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
rows.claim: A scholar recounts joining two ascetics who vowed to eat nothing made by a creature; when he left their cave for Tarsus to teach, one said he had broken the pact and forfeited gifts they received: traversing earth instantly, walking on water, and concealing themselves at will.
rows.anchor: وعن بعض أهل العلم كنت بالمصيصة فإذا برجلين يتكلمان في الخلوة مع الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tale warns that choosing worldly benefit—even teaching, despite its religious form—can cost divine gifts; a seeker in retreat must shed every name, status, and outward identity.
rows.anchor: اختار ما عند الناس فحرم مما عند الله من الكرامات والكفالات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here shaqāʾ commonly means exertion, illustrated by the hard labor of a horse trainer who makes a foal rideable; the saying serves as a proverb.
rows.anchor: الشقاء شائع بمعنى التعب ومن أشقى من رائض المهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was not sent to exhaust himself grieving over Quraysh’s unbelief: his duty was to convey, which he had done, and their later belief was not his responsibility.
rows.anchor: لتتعب بفرط تأسك على كفر قريش إذ ما عليك إلا البلاغ وقد فعلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also rejects excessive ascetic exercise and night vigil: the Prophet was sent with a tolerant, upright religion, not to stand all night until his legs were injured.
rows.anchor: أو بكثرة الرياضة وكثرة التهجد والقيام على ساق إذ ما بعثت إلا بالحنيفية السمحة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Qur’an was revealed to make the Prophet happy through embodying its character, and to make the inhabitants of the heavens and earth happy through his noble character.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا أو العقبى بل أنزلناه على قلبك لتسعد بتخلقك بخلقه

rows.speaker: أبو جهل والنضر بن الحارث
rows.claim: Bursevī says Abū Jahl and al-Naḍr b. al-Ḥārith called the Prophet wretched for leaving his forefathers’ religion and claimed the Qur’an would make him miserable.
rows.anchor: فإن أبا جهل والنضر بن الحارث قالا له : إنك شقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against their charge, Islam and the Qur’an lead to every success and happiness; the unbelievers’ condition is misery itself.
rows.anchor: بأن دين الإسلام وهذا القرآن هو السلم إلى نيل كل فوز والسبب في درك كل سعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadhkiratan is accusative as the purpose of revelation, coordinated in meaning with the negated tashaqqā through a disconnected exception; one verb has two purposes only by substitution or coordination.
rows.anchor: نصب على أنه مفعول له لأنزلنا معطوف على تشقى بحسب المعنى بعد نفيه بطريق الاستدراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an was sent as reminder and admonition for those God knows will fear when reminded and warned, rather than to burden the Prophet in its delivery.
rows.anchor: ولكن تذكيرا وموعظة لمن يعلم الله منه أن يخشى بالتذكرة والتخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although reminder and proclamation are universal, the verse singles out those who benefit from them, consistent with the Qur’an being a warning to all worlds.
rows.anchor: وتخصيصها بهم مع عموم التذكرة والتبليغ لقوله تعالى : {ليكون للعالمين نذيرا}

rows.speaker: الكبير
rows.claim: Al-Kabīr says the Messenger is included among those who fear, indeed foremost in fear and in receiving the reminder.
rows.anchor: قال في "الكبير" ويدخل تحت قوله : {لمن يخشى} الرسول

words: تنزيلا ممن خلق الأرض والسماوات العلى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanzīlan means that the Qur’an was sent down as a true sending-down; min is attached to it, and khalaqa means bringing from nonexistence into existence.
rows.anchor: {تنزيلا} أي : نزل القرآن تنزيلا {ممن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth and the high heavens are specified because they sustain the world and are its foundations; earth comes first because it is nearer to the senses and more apparent.
rows.anchor: تخصيص خلقهما لأنهما قوام العالم وأصوله وتقديم الأرض لكونها أقرب إلى الحس وأظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿUlā is the feminine plural of al-aʿlā; describing the heavens as high points to the greatness of the Creator’s power in raising them.
rows.anchor: ووصف السموات بالعلى وهو جمع العليا تأنيث الأعلى للدلالة على عظم قدرة خلقها بعلوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coordination is genus with genus, since both definite nouns denote classes, not a plural coordinated with a singular in a less apt agreement.
rows.anchor: وعطف السموات على الأرض من عطف الجنس على الجنس لأن التعريف مصروف إلى الجنس

words: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All that is in the heavens and earth, within them or constituting them, and between them belongs solely to God, who owns and governs it without partner or independent co-owner.
rows.anchor: سواء كان ذلك بالجزئية منهما أو بالحلول فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What lies between them includes beings continuously in the air, such as air and clouds, and those there most of the time, such as birds.
rows.anchor: دائما كالهواء والسحاب أو أكثريا كالطير

words: له ما في السماوات وما في الأرض
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s sole ownership entails disposal, giving and taking life, and annihilation of everything mentioned.
rows.anchor: ملكا وتصرفا وإحياء وإمانة وإعداما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tharā is moist, damp soil; the word may refer to the earth itself or to damp soil beneath its dry surface.
rows.anchor: الثرى التراب الندي أي : الرطب والأرض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: When tharā is taken as the world’s outermost surface, authorities variously name what lies below as a bull, fish, rock, sea, or air; another account places damp soil five hundred years beneath the earth, whose underside only God knows.
rows.anchor: هو إما الثور أو الحوت أو الصخرة أو البحر أو الهواء على اختلاف الروايات وقال بعضهم

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī reports a cosmology of earth on an angel, then rock, ox, whale, ocean, Hell, wind, and a vessel of darkness; human knowledge reaches only the veil above tharā, while God alone knows beneath it.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (زمين بردوش فرشته ايست وقدمين فرشته بر صخره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the earths rest on Nun, whose head and tail meet beneath the Throne; the sea rests on the green rock of Luqmān 31:16, on an ox’s horn, then tharā. The ox’s mouth swallows the unified seas, which dry inside it; only God knows below tharā.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إن الأرضين على ظهر النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To make the saying aloud is to announce God’s remembrance and invocation; the following explanation is continued in the next segment.
rows.anchor: {وإن تجهر بالقول} أي : إن تعلن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is independent of public remembrance and invocation, since He knows both the secret and what is more hidden.
rows.anchor: فاعلم أنه تعالى غني عن جهرك وإعلانك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense denotes continuous knowledge in every age; divine knowledge transcends time and place, and change belongs to its objects, not to knowledge itself.
rows.anchor: علمهما منه مستمر دائم وذلك أن علمه تعالى منزه عن الزمان كما هو منزه عن المكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirr is what one conceals; the indefinite akhfā intensifies hiddenness and can mean a thought kept from others, an unspoken thought, or a thought one will later form without anticipating it.
rows.anchor: والسر واحد الأسرار وهو ما يكتم ومنه أسر الحديث إذا أخفاه وتنكير أخفى للمبالغة في الخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may prohibit loudness, as in 7:205, or guide worshippers that audible dhikr serves inner imprint, focus, resistance to distraction, humility, awakening others, and spreading blessings and witnesses.
rows.anchor: وهذا إما نهي عن الجهر كقوله تعالى : {واذكر ربك في نفسك

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: At Khaybar, after people raised their voices with takbīr and tahlīl from a valley, the Prophet told them to be gentle because they call One who hears and is near, not a deaf or absent being.
rows.anchor: وجاء أنه عليه السلام لما توجه إلى خيبر أشرف الناس على واد فرفعوا أصواتهم بالتكبير

rows.speaker: إنسان العيون
rows.claim: The prohibition is reconciled with the Prophet’s command to raise voices in talbiya by limiting it to excessive loudness beyond ordinary levels that can cause harm.
rows.anchor: المنهى عنه هنا الرفع الخارج عن العادة الذي ربما آذى بدليل قوله عليه السلام أربعوا على أنفسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet also restrained loudness to hide plans from enemies and suit spiritually realized companions’ preference for moderation; Sufis use audible dhikr to intimidate the ego and Satan and drive away whispering, with louder voices for necessity.
rows.anchor: ولذا اعتاد الصوفية بجهر الذكر تهييبا لهما وطردا للوسوسة

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The philosophers recommend that rulers speak loudly so listeners feel awe and the words make a stronger impression.
rows.anchor: وقد اختار الحكماء للسلطان جهارة الصوت في كلامه ليكون أهيب لسامعيه وأوقع في قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration is a substitute for what is revealed and demonstrates that knowledge of foundational creed precedes practical branches: divine oneness comes before worship.
rows.anchor: وهو بدل من يوص دال على تقدم علم الأصول على الفروع فإن التوحيد من مسائل الأصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God alone is deity, worship must be devoted to Him alone, without associating anyone with Him.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان كذلك {فاعبدنى} فخصني بالعبادة والتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is singled out after the general command to worship because of its special merit.
rows.anchor: {وأقم الصلواة} من عطف الخاص على العام لفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If remembrance is the object of the genitive, the prayer is performed so that the worshipper remembers God; proper remembrance engages tongue, heart, and limbs, all of which prayer gathers.
rows.anchor: {لذكرى} من إضافة المصدر إلى مفعوله أي : لتذكرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, remembrance may be a subject genitive: pray so that God remembers you through recompense.
rows.anchor: أو من إضافته إلى فاعله أي لأذكرك بالإثابة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The verse inwardly calls for lasting intimate converse and presence with God, giving up the self to attain His continuous remembrance through theophany and annihilation of renewed existence.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : وأدم المناجات والمحاضرة معي ببذل الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks the essence of the named thing, its reality by which it is what it is, as when one asks what Zayd is and answers that he is a human being.
rows.anchor: السؤال بما تلك عن ماهية المسمى أي : حقيقته

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī places the address after Moses removed his sandals in the sacred valley.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ون موسى نعلين بيرون كرد در وادي مقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is an interrogative predicate of tilka, which points to the staff; this parsing fits Moses’ answer better than reversing the construction.
rows.anchor: فما استفهامية في حيز الرفع بالخبرية لتلك المشار إليها أي : العصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The specification of the right hand avoids possible confusion if Moses held a ring or another object in his left hand; a generic reference to his hand might have left him unsure what was asked.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل بيدك لاحتمال أن يكون في يساره شيء مثل الخاتم ونحوه فلو أجمل إليه لتحير في الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls it my staff to establish that it is in his right hand and prepare for the later actions attributed to him.
rows.anchor: نسبها إلى نفسه تحقيقا لوجه كونها بيمينه وتمهيدا لما يعقبه من الأفاعيل المنسوبة إليه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He leans on the staff when weary during travel, while walking, and while standing near the flock at pasture.
rows.anchor: اعتمد عليها عند الإعياء في الطريق وحال المشي وحين الوقوف على رأس القطيع في المرعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hashsh means striking foliage with a staff so it falls; Moses knocks leaves from trees onto the sheep’s heads for them to eat.
rows.anchor: يقال هش الورق يهشه ويهشه خبطه بعصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʾārib is plural of maʾriba, with rāʾ read with fatḥa or ḍamma; ukhrā is feminine to match the pause-ending cadence.
rows.anchor: جمع مأربة بفتح الراء وضمها وهي الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond leaning and shaking down leaves, the staff serves as a shoulder pole for a bow, quiver, milk pail, and water flask, carries provisions, and provides company on the road.
rows.anchor: إذا سار ألقاها على عاتقه وعلق بها قوسه وكنانته وحلابه ومطهرته وحمل عليها زاده وتحدثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its forked end and hook could bend or twist branches to break them; a point at the bottom could be planted to draw water, and its forks could act as a bucket in a well, with the staff extending a short rope.
rows.anchor: وكان لها شعبتان ومحجن فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن وإذا حاول كسره لواه بالشعبتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff could light the night like a candle, defend Moses against enemies and predators, drive away vermin, and support a cloak as a shade in the wilderness.
rows.anchor: وإذا تعرضت لغنمه السباع قاتل بها وتطرد الهوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff was twelve cubits by Moses’ measure, made from a myrtle tree in the Garden, and entrusted to Shuʿayb by an angel in human form.
rows.anchor: وكانت اثني عشر ذراعا بذراعه عليه السلام من عود آس من شجر الجنة استودعها عند شعيب ملك من الملائكة في صورة إنسان

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī says the staff came from the Garden, had two forks, a hook and a lower point, was named ʿAlīq, and passed from Adam to Shuʿayb and then Moses.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (آن عصا ازوب مرد بهشت بود طول اوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff symbolizes prophets as shepherds of people, who resemble livestock needing guidance and protection from Satan’s wolves and the ego’s lion; people must follow their direction and serve them.
rows.anchor: وفي العصا إشارة إلى أن الأنبياء عليهم السلام رعاة الخلق والخلق مثل البهائم محتاجون إلى الرعي والكلاءة

rows.speaker: الحافظ
rows.claim: Ḥāfiẓ’s couplet says the shepherd of the valley of Ayman reaches his aim through nine years of devoted service to Shuʿayb.
rows.anchor: شبان وادى ايمن كهى رسد بمراد كه ند سال بجان خدمت شعيب كند

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعرفة
rows.claim: Some knowers identify the staff with the tranquil soul, which effaces illusions and imaginings; its serpent form is receptive to faith, as jinn once appeared as snakes in Medina and people were told not to kill them.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أهل المعرفة لما كانت العصا صورة النفس المطمئنة المفنية للموهومات والمتخيلات

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعرفة
rows.claim: In this reading, Moses relies on the soul for hidden aims and acquired perfections gained through bodily striving and spiritual discipline; his flock represents his limbs, senses, and natural and bodily powers.
rows.anchor: أي : أستعين بها على مطالبي في السر {وأهش بها على غنمى} أي : على رعايا أعضائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through struggle and discipline the soul repents, and disobedience turns into obedience, citing God’s promise to replace the repentant’s evil deeds with good deeds.
rows.anchor: فإذا جاهدت وارتاضت وأنابت إلى ربها انقلبت المعصية التي هي السيئة طاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God knows all, He asks so observers first identify an insignificant staff, then witness the extraordinary miracles made from it, like a goldsmith displaying an iron blank before turning it into armor.
rows.anchor: قلنا فائدته أن من أراد أن يظهر من الحقير شيئا نفيسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed Persian couplet counsels abandoning base worldly existence to find love’s alchemy and become gold.
rows.anchor: دست ازمس وجود ومردان ره بشوى تا كيمياى عشق بيابى وزر شوى

rows.speaker: المولى الجامي
rows.claim: Jāmī says knowledge without action is poison and futile: one who knows alchemy has gained nothing unless he turns his own copper into gold.
rows.anchor: وقال المولى الجامي : وكسب علم كردى در عمل كوش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāla is a resumption answering an implied question about what God did next.
rows.anchor: {قال} استئناف بياني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff became a male serpent that swallowed rocks and stones in its path, had eyes blazing like fire and loudly grinding fangs, and stretched forty or eighty cubits between its jaws; Moses fled from the terrifying sight.
rows.anchor: روي أنها انقلبت ثعبانا ذكرا يبتلع كل شيء يمر به من صخر وحجر وعيناه تتقدان كالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses feared because fear and flight from snakes and similar creatures belong to ordinary human nature.
rows.anchor: لما رآه كذلك خاف ونفر لأن الخوف والهرب من الحيات ونحوها من طباع البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked why Moses feared the staff while Abraham did not fear the fire, Bursevī says Abraham was more firmly established; God removed Moses’ initial fear, enabling him to take the staff and reach Abraham’s state of firmness.
rows.anchor: لأن الخليل كان أشد تمكينا إذ فرق بين بداية الحال ونهايتها وقد أزال الله هذا الخوف من موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet likewise first feared Gabriel, then became ready to see him in his true form on the Miʿrāj, as described in 53:13–14.
rows.anchor: أول ما جاءه جبريل خافه فرجع من الجبل مرتعدا ثم كان من أمره ما كان

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading says Moses first believed the staff held benefits, then feared its harm; taking it without fear teaches that God alone brings harm and benefit, so fear and hope belong to Him alone.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" {خذها ولا تخف} يعني كنت تحسب أن لك فيها المنافع

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: A Mathnawī couplet teaches that whoever fears God and adopts piety is feared by jinn and humans, while one who beholds God need fear no creature.
rows.anchor: وفي "المثنوي" : هركه ترسيد از حق وتقوى كزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīra is a pattern or kind of going, figuratively a way or form; the accusative follows removal of a preposition and denotes the staff’s original shape.
rows.anchor: السيرة فعلة من السير أي : نوع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses put his hand in the serpent’s mouth; it returned to a staff, with his hand in the familiar place between its forks. The sign prepared him not to fear its transformation before Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: فوضع يده في فم الحية فصارت عصا كما كانت ويده في شعبتيها في الموضع الذي يضعها فيه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A hadith says that a person who failed to pay zakat will be brought with that wealth appearing as a serpent.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "يجاء لصاحب المال الذي لم يؤد زكاته بذلك المال على صورة ثعبان"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every body, including a nonphysical one, has a spirit; each deed, trait, or attribute has a fitting form that becomes perceptible in the next life, as 6:108 says God will show people what they did.
rows.anchor: لكل جسد روحا ولو كان معنويا ولكل عمل وخلق ووصف صورة معتدلة في الدنيا تتحو صورة محسوسة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love of wealth is a powerful trait of the commanding soul, which resembles a harmful serpent and becomes an alarming form around its owner’s neck when inner realities are exposed.
rows.anchor: ولما كان حب المال من أشد صفات النفس الأمارة التي هي في صورة ثعبان ضار لا جرم يظهر يوم تبلى السرائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the heart is purified from love of wealth and comes to love spending in God’s way, that disposition takes a beautiful form suited to its good deeds; the same analogy applies to other traits.
rows.anchor: فإذا تزكى موسى القلب من حب المال وأحب بذله في سبيل الله جاء في صورة حسنة يهواها مناسبة لما عمل به من الخيرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expanding the breast is a divine gift to prophets and perfected saints; the Prophet received the fullest share, literally and inwardly, through chest-opening in youth, at forty for the burdens of mission, and on the Miʿrāj for divine secrets.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن شرح الصدر من نعم الله تعالى على الأنبياء وكمل الأولياء وقد أخذ منه نبينا عليه السلام الحظ الأوفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s childhood chest-opening removed the clot described as the devil’s share and touch, and he was washed in a golden basin; later expansions prepared him to bear the mission and receive divine secrets.
rows.anchor: إذ شق صدره في صباوته وألقي عنه العلقة التي هي حظ الشيطان ومغمزه وغسل في طست من الذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks God to ease the mission of conveying the message by creating the means and removing obstacles.
rows.anchor: سهل علي أمر التبليغ بإحداث الأسباب ورفع الموانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥlil means open or undo; ʿuqda is a speech impediment, and its indefinite form indicates that the impediment was slight.
rows.anchor: {من لسانى} متعلق بالفعل وتنكير عقدة يدل على قلتها في نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds sayings that a person is defined by the heart and tongue, the two small organs; without a tongue the person is only an inarticulate sign or represented image.
rows.anchor: ما الإنسان لولا اللسان الابهمية مرسلة أو صورة ممثلة والمرؤ بأصغريه قلبه ولسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhahā means to go or depart and is used for both physical things and meanings, as in Abraham’s going to his Lord and the terror leaving Abraham.
rows.anchor: والذهاب المضي يقال ذهب بالشيء وأذهبه ويستعمل ذلك في الأعيان والمعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction implies that Aaron too should go; he is coordinated in ellipsis because he was away from Moses at that time.
rows.anchor: أي : وليذهب أخوك هارون حسبما استدعيت عطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Brotherhood may be full, half, or by nursing, and is also figuratively used for people sharing a qibla, religion, craft, dealings, affection, or another affinity.
rows.anchor: ويستعار الأخ لكل مشارك لغيره في القبلة أو في الدين أو في صنعة أو في معاملة أو في مودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: My signs means God’s miracles; the preposition marks accompaniment, since Moses and Aaron go to Pharaoh equipped with the signs to carry out the prophetic mission, not merely to be delivered to him.
rows.anchor: بمعجزاتي والباء للمصاحبة لا للتعدية إذ المراد ذهابهما إلى فرعون ملتبسين بالآيات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the signs as the nine sent down to Moses, even though some had not yet occurred.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يريد الآيات التسع التي أنزلت عليه وإن كان وقوع بعضها بالفعل مترقبا بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural may be honorific for the staff and hand, or may reflect al-Khalīl’s view that the minimum plural is two.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الجمع للتعظيم والمراد العصا واليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taniyā means do not slack or flag; wany and its listed forms denote weakness or slackening.
rows.anchor: من ونى يني ونيا فهو وإن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They must persist in remembering God with tongue and heart in every state; remembrance enables every purpose, and neglect in other affairs results from neglect of God’s remembrance.
rows.anchor: {فى ذكرى} أي : في مداومته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder echoes Moses’ earlier prayer that the two might glorify and remember God much.
rows.anchor: وهو تذكير لقوله : {كى نسبحك كثيرا * ونذكرك كثيرا}

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation is that remembering God’s majesty makes all else seem small, so the soul grows strong and does not fear anyone else or weaken in its aim.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الحكمة في هذا التكليف أن من ذكر جلال الله تعالى وعظمته

rows.speaker: حضرة الهدايي
rows.claim: The Jelveti path’s master says beginning with divine oneness before exhortation makes listeners attentive and, by God’s help, makes the admonition effective.
rows.anchor: قال مرجع طريقتنا الجلوتية بالجيم حضرة الهدايى قدس سره التوحيد قبل الوعظ باعث لإصغاء السامعين

rows.speaker: العرائس
rows.claim: Al-ʿArāʾis reads the command as a warning not to become absent from divine witnessing while occupied with God’s work, lest one be fatigued away from God by serving Him.
rows.anchor: وفي "العرائس" : لا تغيبا عن مشاهدتي باشتغالكما بأمري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh left the gathering and went away, then sent to the cities to assemble the magicians.
rows.anchor: ترك الولي والقرب وانصرف عن المجلس وأرسل إلى المدائن لجمع السحرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh gathered the sorcerers and their equipment; kayd is a kind of stratagem or deception.
rows.anchor: ما يكاد به من السحرة وأدواتهم والكيد ضرب من الاحتيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He came to the appointed place; the sequence marker hints that he delayed rather than hurrying there.
rows.anchor: وفي كلمة التراخي إيماء إلى أنه لم يسارع إليه بل أتاه بعد تأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording answers the implied question of what Moses did when Pharaoh arrived with the magicians: he spoke to them as an adviser.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل فماذا صنع موسى عند إتيان فرعون مع السحرة فقيل قال لهم بطريق النصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wailukum originally invokes ruin, as if saying may God bind you to misery; here it rebukes and restrains, urging them to stop fabricating.
rows.anchor: أصله الدعاء بالهلاك بمعنى ألزمكم الله ويلا يعني عذابا وهلاكا والمراد هنا الزجر والردع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses warns them not to claim falsely that the coming signs are magic, and not to associate partners with God; iftirāʾ is deliberate falsehood.
rows.anchor: بأن تدعو أن الآيات التي ستظهر على يدي سحر أو لا تشركوا مع الله أحدا والافتراء التقول والكذب عن عمد

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt specifies the warning: do not perform magic under the guise of a miracle, falsely claiming God gave you what He gave the prophets.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات" : قال موسى للسحرة {ويلكم لا تفتروا على الله كذبا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yusḥitkum means that God will annihilate and uproot them through the torment.
rows.anchor: يقال اسحت الشيء أعدمه واستأصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened torment is immense and beyond measure.
rows.anchor: {بعذاب} هائل لا يقادر قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayba is missing one’s aim; anyone who invents a lie against God, whoever they are and however they do it, will fail.
rows.anchor: الخيبة فوت المطلب أي : (بى بهره ونا اميدماند) {من افترى}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening fa is explanatory of an omitted premise; ajmiʿū comes from ijmāʿ, to settle a matter decisively by uniting one’s judgment.
rows.anchor: الفاء فصيحة واجمعوا من الإجماع يقال أجمع الأمر إذا أحكمه وعزم عليه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib notes that ijmāʿ is most often used for a gathering achieved through deliberation and planning.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : أكثر ما يقال فيما يكون جمعا يتوصل إليه بالتدبير والفكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since Moses and Aaron supposedly intend to expel them, the magicians should plan together how to remove these rivals, unite their scheme, and act with one purpose.
rows.anchor: فازمعوا مكركم وحيلكم في رفع هذا المزاحم واجعلوه مجمعا عليه بحيث لا يتخلف عنه واحد منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading derives the verb from gathering: collect and properly arrange the instruments of sorcery; 20:60’s account of Pharaoh gathering his scheme supports this sense.
rows.anchor: وقرىء فاجمعوا من الجمع ويعضده قوله تعالى : {فجمع كيده}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are to come lined up and assembled at the meeting place to inspire greater awe and keep their affair organized.
rows.anchor: مصطفين في الموعد ومجتمعين ليكون أشد لهيبتكم وانظم لأمركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They arrived in seventy lines, each containing a thousand people.
rows.anchor: فجاءوا في سبعين صفا كل صف ألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaff is arranging things along a straight line, as with people or trees, and can also denote those aligned or the active participle.
rows.anchor: والصف أن يجعل الشيء على خط مستو كالناس والأشجار ونحو ذلك وقد يجعل بمعنى الصاف

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād supposes the meeting place was spacious: Moses addressed the magicians from one edge, they debated at another, then they were told to assemble in its center.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : لعل الموعد كان مكانا متسعا خاطبهم موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aflāḥ means attaining the goal; istaʿlā can mean blameworthy pursuit of superiority or noble elevation, so the verse admits victory or high standing among people.
rows.anchor: والاستعلاء قد يكون طلب العلو المذموم

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: Al-Irshād says their hoped-for gain was Pharaoh’s promised pay and favor; the winner may mean all of them or whichever individual prevails, exhorting each to exert maximum effort.
rows.anchor: يريدون بالمطلوب ما وعدهم فرعون من الأجر والتقريب وبمن غلب أنفسهم جميعا أو من غلب منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forbidden arts and means such as magic are blameworthy when used to gain worldly wealth rather than the hereafter or God; prohibited means will not yield spiritual rank, and only toil remains.
rows.anchor: المنهى من العلوم والأسباب كالسحر ونحوه ما يتقرب به إلى الدنيا وجمع طامها لا إلى الآخرة
